title: Huichihuayán Spring (Nacimiento de Huichihuayán): The Hidden Gem of the Huasteca
metaTitle: Huichihuayán Spring: The Hidden Gem of the Huasteca
metaDescription: What it's like to swim at Huichihuayán Spring, the blue spring in Huehuetlán near Xilitla: what to expect, practical tips and the tour route that stops there.
excerpt: Huichihuayán Spring is a clear blue spring in Huehuetlán, near Xilitla, where you can swim in natural pools. What to expect, the best season, entry price and how to get there from Ciudad Valles.
contentHtml:
Huichihuayán Spring (Nacimiento de Huichihuayán) is a spring of clear blue water that flows out of the mountains in the municipality of Huehuetlán, Huasteca Potosina, and it's known as one of the most striking springs (ojos de agua) in northeastern Mexico. Many travelers come to the region without knowing this natural spot is just minutes from the main highway, and they end up missing it for lack of up-to-date information. Getting to know Huichihuayán Spring with accurate information makes the difference between an improvised visit and a day well spent.

Here we tell you what it's like to swim in the spring and what to expect. Up-to-date admission, hours and directions are on the Huichihuayán Spring page.

In this article you'll find everything you need to plan your visit: how to get there from Ciudad Valles, how much admission costs in 2026, what you can do and the best season to enjoy this blue Huasteca spring. The November-to-May season is the busiest, thanks to how clear the water is in the dry season.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: November 2026. Before you pack, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina.

How do you get to Huichihuayán Spring from Ciudad Valles?

Route from Ciudad Valles: distance and road access

Huichihuayán Spring is south of Ciudad Valles on the Mexico–Laredo federal highway. When you reach the town of Huehuetlán, a 3 km paved stretch leads straight to the site, with signs you can see from the main road. The drive takes about 80 minutes in 2026, depending on traffic.

If you'd rather not drive, Huichihuayán is one of the stops on our Surrealist Route (Ruta Surrealista), which costs $1,400 MXN per person with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles (from Valles, $400 MXN more per booking).

What public transportation is there to get to Huichihuayán?

Buses leave Ciudad Valles for Huehuetlán in the mornings; a ticket costs about $80 to $100 MXN each way in 2026. Once in town, you can take a mototaxi or walk the remaining 3 km to the spring. It's best to leave before 9:00 a.m. to catch the best light and the smallest crowds.

If you're planning a longer getaway, check out the 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary we put together with routes checked by our local guides.

Activities and prices at Huichihuayán Spring in 2026

Swimming in this Huasteca spring: the experience and real conditions

You're free to swim in the pools, and the local committee rents life jackets to anyone who needs one. The water is clearest between November and April, when the rains don't change the color of the spring.

An honest warning: in the rainy season — June to October — the water level rises and the current can become unpredictable, so swimming without supervision isn't recommended. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina with certified guides for this season.

How much does it cost to visit Huichihuayán Spring?

Admission is $30 MXN per person in 2026, paid at the booth at the site. You can bring your own food and drinks, and inside there's food for sale made by the local community.

If you're traveling on a tight budget, reading how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026 is a good place to start.

Tips before visiting Huichihuayán Spring

A couple of hours of preparation saves you from the most common setbacks. These tips are based on the experience of the groups we take around the Huasteca Potosina every season.

  • Check the hours before you go: It's open from 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; even so, contact the site's committee through its Facebook page before you leave to confirm it's open that day.
  • Pick the best season: November to May brings the clearest water and ideal conditions; see the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.
  • Bring cash: Admission is $30 MXN and paid in cash; there are no card terminals on site.
  • The right clothes and gear: Bring a swimsuit, water sandals, biodegradable sunscreen and a change of dry clothes for the trip back; the ground near the spring can be slippery.

Frequently asked questions about Huichihuayán Spring

Can you swim at Huichihuayán Spring?

Yes, you can swim in the pools. The local committee rents life jackets. The safest season, with the clearest water, is November to May 2026. In the rainy season the current picks up and you should take extra care.

How much is admission to Huichihuayán Spring?

Admission is $30 MXN per person in 2026, paid in cash at the booth at the site. You can bring your own food. Our Surrealist Route, which stops at the spring, costs $1,400 MXN per person with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles (from Valles, $400 MXN more per booking).

How do you get to Huichihuayán from Ciudad Valles, and how long does it take?

Huichihuayán is south of Ciudad Valles on the Mexico–Laredo highway. By car, the drive takes about 80 minutes. From Huehuetlán, 3 km of paved road lead to the spring. By public transportation, there are buses from Ciudad Valles for about $80 to $100 MXN.

Is Huichihuayán Spring safe for families?

Yes, Huichihuayán Spring is suitable for families with kids in the dry season. Use life jackets for the little ones and stay away from areas with stronger current. To plan a complete family route, see our guide to the Huasteca Potosina with kids.
